bihar_raw_news.title: Government disburses Rs 36754 crore under PLI schemes since 2020 - The Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 25, 2026 Government disburses Rs 36,754 crore under PLI schemes since 2020 Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Press Trust of India Representational image, file photo (2015): Prime Minister Narendra Modi meets workers at a mobile and electronics manufacturing hub in Tirupati. Photo: Prime Minister’s Office / Government of India (GODL-India). New Delhi, Sep 25 (PTI) The government has disbursed Rs 36,754 crore to beneficiary companies under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes since the launch in 2020 till June 30 this year, with the largest amount of Rs 19,090.98 crore released to large-scale electronics manufacturing, according to the DPIIT. The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) data showed that Rs 1,400 crore was disbursed in this fiscal year until June 30. The disbursal was Rs 15,519 crore in 2025-26 and Rs 10,114 crore in 2024-25. The government launched the schemes in 2020 for 14 sectors, with an approved outlay of Rs 1.91 lakh crore, to enhance manufacturing capabilities, attract investment, promote exports, generate employment, and reduce import dependence. While Rs 6,662 crore was disbursed to the pharma sector, Rs 3,271.440 crore and Rs 3,174.15 crore were released to the beneficiary firms of food products and auto and auto components segments, respectively, as on June this year. Other disbursals included Rs 2,796 crore for telecom and networking products; Rs 593 crore for white goods; Rs 386 crore for textiles; Rs 236 crore for speciality steel; Rs 93 crore for drones and drone components; Rs 98 crore for IT hardware; and Rs 88 crore for bulk drugs beneficiary companies. There were no disbursals in the Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) battery sector. The DPIIT added that as on June 30, 2026, the schemes have resulted in actual investment of Rs 2.58 lakh crore, against which production/sales of Rs 23.79 lakh crore and exports of Rs 15.53 lakh crore have been recorded. "These schemes have led to the employment generation of over 14.57 lakh (direct and indirect) along with Rs 36,754 crore of cumulative incentives disbursed so far,” it said. "Major global players such as Siemens, Wipro GE and Philips have participated in technology-transfer projects, enabling domestic manufacture of CT/MRI systems, cath labs and ultrasonography equipment. PLI beneficiaries have generated Rs 6,475 crore in domestic sales, with Rs 560 crore exports and Rs 1,400 crore revenue from implants,” it said. In the sector, global brands including Dell, HP, Lenovo, Acer, ASUS and HPE have initiated domestic manufacturing, directly or through Indian EMS (electronic manufacturing services) partners. Further, in the speciality steel sector, the ministry said leading companies including JSW, Jindal Odisha, Tata Steel and AMNS have invested over Rs 19,000 crore, supporting domestic production of value-added speciality steel for automobiles, defence, capital goods and renewable energy, and reducing dependence on imports. Further under the PLI schemes, cumulative investment in 14 sectors stood at Rs 2,58,835 crore as of June 2026, according to DPIIT data. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary inaugurates tent city, reviews Pitru Paksha Mela arrangements in Gaya
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary inaugurates tent city, reviews Pitru Paksha Mela arrangements in Gaya ANI | Updated: Sep 25, 2026 18:18 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Gaya ( Bihar ) [India], September 25 (ANI): Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary visited Gaya on the occasion of the Pitru Paksha Mela, offered prayers at the Vishnupad Temple and inspected arrangements at Dev Ghat to review facilities being provided to devotees, according to the Bihar Chief Minister's Office (CMO). The Chief Minister prayed for the peace, prosperity and well-being of the state and inaugurated the tent city set up for devotees during the Pitru Paksha Mela. He directed officials to ensure better facilities and arrangements for visitors. Choudhary said that a large number of devotees from across the country and abroad visit Gaya during Pitru Paksha, and ensuring that they receive proper facilities and return with a positive experience is the government's priority. " Bihar has a tradition of 'Atithi Devo Bhava'. Devotees and guests arriving for the Pitru Paksha Mela should be welcomed with full respect and honour," the Chief Minister said. He instructed officials to maintain better arrangements for devotees, including facilities at ghats, accommodation, drinking water, cleanliness and security. Addressing the inauguration programme of the tent city, Choudhary said the Pitru Paksha Mela represents faith, respect and gratitude towards ancestors in Sanatan culture. He said devotees from across the world visit Gaya for pind daan and tarpan rituals, and the state government is working to provide them with improved facilities. The Chief Minister said arrangements are being made for devotees at both Punpun and Gaya during the Pitru Paksha period. He added that technology and mobile applications are being used to assist devotees arriving from different states, with information being provided in their respective languages. He said facilities in Gaya are being expanded in view of the increasing number of visitors. The Vishnupad Corridor project will involve a total expenditure of Rs 3,500 crore by the Centre and state governments, including Rs 2,500 crore proposed for the corridor development. He said the project is among the biggest initiatives undertaken for the development of a temple in the state. Choudhary also highlighted plans for industrial development in Bihar , stating that an Integrated Manufacturing Cluster (IMC) is being initiated in Bodh Gaya . Around Rs 20,000 crore worth of industrial investment is expected to begin taking shape from October this year, creating new employment opportunities and boosting economic activities. He said work is also underway on a project worth around Rs 1,000 crore to bring water from the Son river to the Falgu river, which will improve irrigation and water availability in Gaya and nearby areas. On air connectivity, the Chief Minister said Gaya Airport is among the major airports of Bihar and efforts are being made to connect Gaya with Indonesia, Bangkok, Gulf countries and other key global destinations. Ceigall India Limited has approved a comprehensive investment package for its subsidiary, Ceigall Sahebganj Bettiah Highway Limited, to finance a national highway construction project in Bihar. The approval, granted by the Management Committee of the Board of Directors on September 25, 2026, covers equity, loans, securities, and guarantees. This expands upon the previously disclosed ₹61.93 crore equity infusion, indicating a multi-instrument approach to meeting the project's fund requirements. Project details and structure The subsidiary serves as the Project Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) for the construction of the Sahebganj-Areraj-Bettiah section of National Highway 139W. The project involves 4-laning of a total length of 78.942 km on a Hybrid Annuity Mode basis. The National Highways Authority of India awarded the contract to Ceigall Infra Projects Private Limited (CIPPL), a wholly owned subsidiary of Ceigall India, via a Letter of Award dated February 11, 2026. The project is divided into two sections: Section 1: Sahebganj to Areraj (38.362 km) Section 2: Areraj to Bettiah (40.580 km) Investment breakdown The total consideration for the initial equity acquisition remains ₹61,93,00,000 (₹61.93 crore). The SPV was incorporated on February 17, 2026, with an authorized and paid-up share capital of ₹1 lakh initially. What the numbers show The shift from a standalone equity infusion to a broader mix including loans, securities, and guarantees reflects the typical capital structure for Hybrid Annuity Mode projects. While the ₹61.93 crore equity component establishes the developer's skin in the game, the inclusion of debt instruments and guarantees suggests the company is preparing to leverage external financing to complete the 78.942 km stretch. The disparity between the SPV's nominal initial capital of ₹1 lakh and the significant approved funding highlights the scale-up required for such infrastructure commitments. bihar_raw_news.title: Raxaul-Haldia Expressway: Proposed corridor between North Bihar and West Bengal may ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Raxaul-Haldia Expressway: Proposed corridor between North Bihar and West Bengal may cut travel time by half The travel time between Raxaul and Haldia is expected to take just 9 to 10 hours after the corridor is complete. By CNBCTV18.com September 25, 2026, 3:14:46 PM IST (Published) 2 Min Read Work on the proposed Raxaul-Haldia Expressway is progressing rapidly. Set to pass through the states of Bihar, Jharkhand, and West Bengal, the expressway will prove crucial for India’s trade with Nepal. It will also connect parts of Bihar to the Bay of Bengal. The project will connect major commercial and industrial hubs in the three states, including Champaran (Raxaul/Motihari), Muzaffarpur, Begusarai, Khagaria, Munger, Jamui, Deoghar, Dumka, Jamtara, West Bardhaman, East Medinipur, and West Medinipur, as per Jagran. Why the Raxaul-Haldia Expressway is important The expressway will end in West Bengal’s Haldia, an important hub for maritime trade. The 719-kilometre-long corridor will connect Haldia with Bihar’s Raxaul city, which is crucial for the trade between India and Nepal, as per News18 Hindi. Improved connectivity between the two areas could strengthen the movement of goods. After the construction of the corridor, the travel time between Raxaul and Haldia is expected to go down from 17-18 hours to just nine to 10 hours. The access-controlled expressway will be able to handle speeds of up to 120 km/h. Presently, goods from Nepal have to use different routes to reach different parts of India. Once the expressway is complete, it will provide easier connectivity from Raxaul to major industrial and business hubs in eastern India. A direct connection to Haldia Port and the Hooghly River, which flows into the Bay of Bengal, will make shipping more convenient for businesses, reduce freight costs, and improve the logistics network. The corridor will also pass through Deoghar, a major religious site. The improved connectivity will benefit both travellers and local businesses. The project is also expected to boost tourism and import-export businesses in the region. Industrial corridors, warehouses, and food processing parks are being planned along the expressway to transform northern Bihar into an industrial hub. Raxaul-Haldia Expressway progress report Administrative activities for the six-lane corridor have been expedited in approximately 11-12 districts of Bihar, Jagran reported. Land acquisition is underway in 58 revenue villages of Banka district. A 72-km stretch has also been proposed in East Champaran. The construction is expected to finish in 2028. The project has an estimated cost of ₹60,000 crore. Continue Reading Tags expressway

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Proposes 2.5%-4% Storage-Linked RPO Through FY30 - Saur Energy
bihar_raw_news.content: News EV+Storage Bihar Proposes 2.5%-4% Storage-Linked RPO Through FY30 The draft further proposes that obligated entities may meet their specified RPO through consumption of renewable electricity or an energy storage system. Manish Kumar 25 Sep 2026 14:52 IST Follow Us Bihar Proposes 2.5%-4% Storage-Linked RPO Through FY30 Photograph: (AI) Bihar Electricity Regulatory Commission (BERC) has now proposed to introduce a storage-linked component into the Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO), requiring a specified share of the obligation to be met through solar and wind energy along with or through energy storage systems. Advertisment Under the draft Bihar Electricity Regulatory Commission (Renewable Purchase Obligation, its compliance and REC Framework Implementation) (1st Amendment) Regulations, 2026, the storage-linked requirement will start at 2.5% in FY2026-27 and progressively rise to 4% by FY2029-30. Advertisment The proposed trajectory is: Financial Year Storage-linked requirement FY2026-27 2.5% FY2027-28 3.0% FY2028-29 3.5% FY2029-30 4.0% The draft specifies that the requirement will be based on solar/wind energy along with or through storage. Energy Storage Obligation fulfilled through energy stored from renewable sources will also be considered part of the fulfilment of other RPO heads. Advertisment BERC has also proposed periodically reviewing the storage obligation, taking into account the commissioning and operation of pumped-storage projects (PSPs), new commercially viable energy-storage technologies and the cost of battery energy storage systems (BESS). RPO compliance through storage The draft further proposes that obligated entities may meet their specified RPO through consumption of renewable electricity either directly or through an energy storage system. An alternative mechanism would be payment of the buyout price specified by the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC). Draft-SMP-40-2026 Advertisment Under the proposed buyout mechanism, the sums collected would be credited to the Central Energy Conservation Fund under a separate head. The draft proposes that 75% of these amounts be transferred to State Energy Conservation Funds, with the funds used to support development of specified renewable-energy sources and storage capacities. Advertisment RPO calculation for different consumers The draft also proposes specific treatment for open-access consumers and captive users. Open-access consumers classified as obligated entities would have to meet the specified total RPO from renewable energy sources, with their RPO consumption calculated at the point of drawal from the grid. Captive users would include electricity generated and self-consumed in their RPO calculation, excluding auxiliary consumption, subject to specified exclusions. For distribution licensees, the RPO would be calculated based on electricity supplied to consumers within their distribution area, while certain open-access and captive consumption would be excluded from the calculation. The draft amendment is currently open for stakeholder input. BERC has invited comments, suggestions and objections until October 8, 2026, while a public hearing is scheduled for October 13, 2026. The proposed regulations will come into force only after publication in the official Gazette. RPO BERC Advertisment Read the Next Article

bihar_raw_news.title: Assam's Orunodoi Scheme : ₹1500 Festival Boost, One-Time Support Announced for October 2026
bihar_raw_news.content: Assam’s Orunodoi Scheme: ₹1,500 Festival Boost, One-Time Support Announced for October 2026; Check Features, Eligibility and Details By Aishwarya Samant Last Updated: Sep 25, 2026, 14:44 IST Assam’s Orunodoi Scheme offers a ₹1,500 one-time festival boost for October 2026. Check key features, eligibility rules, and updates under this major women-centric financial assistance programme. Assam’s Orunodoi Scheme: ₹1,500 Festival Boost, One-Time Support Announced for October 2026; Check Features, Eligibility and Details Orunodoi Scheme: The Assam government has recently announced an add-on to an old scheme. The government will now give add on financial assistance under the Orunodoi Scheme for October 2026. This announcement is that it will offer a one-time payment of ₹1,500 as a festival relief before Durga Puja 2026. Orundoi is a flagship Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) programme, introduced to support economically weaker women. The scheme has remained one of the largest welfare initiatives in the state by the government. The records say that over 40 lakh beneficiaries are expected to receive the add-on enhanced payout in addition to their regular assistance. This announcement is under the Orunodoi 3.0 scheme of the Assam government. Earlier, beneficiaries also used to receive advance payments during other festivals like Bohag Bihu. The government also provides aid in flood-affected districts under this programme to women. Officials say the scheme plays a key role in poverty reduction and household stability across Assam. What Is The Orunodoi Scheme? The Orunodoi Scheme is a major women-centric welfare programme by Assam government. The scheme is aimed at financial support for poor households through direct cash transfers to women who are eligible. This ensures basic economic security and stability. Key Details About The Orundoi Scheme: The scheme was Launched by Government of Assam on 2 October 2020 Women-centric welfare and financial assistance scheme Targets economically weaker households Funds transferred via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) Money credited directly to women beneficiaries’ bank accounts Covers essential needs like food, healthcare, medicines, electricity Focus on improving financial security and household stability Expanded into Orunodoi 3.0 version One of India’s largest state-level cash transfer schemes Orunodoi Scheme Eligibility This scheme directly targets economically weak and disadvantaged families in Assam. The priority is given to families that are led by only women. This includes widows, unmarried or divorced women and families with someone who is specially abled. How are they segregated? The low income households are identified through state level surveys, these households are also included in the scheme. Then selection is based on socio-economic vulnerability to ensure support reaches those most in need. Beneficiaries must have a valid bank account linked to Aadhaar to receive funds through DBT. The focus remains on including rural and urban poor households across all districts of the state. bihar_raw_news.content: The Bihar Combined Entrance Competitive Examination Board (BCECEB) has released the Round 2 seat allotment results for the Under Graduate Medical Admission Counselling (UGMAC) 2026 on its official portal. This round covers state quota MBBS and BDS seats across government medical colleges in Bihar. If you qualified NEET UG 2026 and registered for UGMAC counselling, you now need to check your allotment, download your letter, and prepare for college reporting. Missing the reporting deadline or failing to carry required documents can result in loss of your seat. Download your Round 2 allotment letter immediately from bceceboard.bihar.gov.in, verify your college and course assignment, and report to your allotted college before the official deadline with all original documents and certificates. What Happened: Round 2 Cutoff and Allotment Released On 25 September 2026, BCECEB published the Round 2 cutoff scores and seat allotment results for UGMAC 2026 on bceceboard.bihar.gov.in. The cutoff data shows the opening and closing NEET UG all-India ranks for each medical and dental college across different categories. The Round 2 allotment covers MBBS, BDS, BAMS, BHMS, and BUMS courses at state quota seats in Bihar government colleges. Candidates who completed their choice-filling within the prescribed window and meet the eligibility criteria are now assigned seats based on their NEET rank, category, and college preferences. Understanding the Cutoff Ranks: How Your NEET Score Determines Your College The cutoff list shows two key numbers for each college and course: the opening rank and the closing rank. The opening rank is the best (lowest) NEET all-India rank that received a seat at that college in Round 2. The closing rank is the worst (highest) NEET rank that was allotted a seat. bihar_raw_news.content: The Bihar Combined Entrance Competitive Examination Board (BCECEB) has released the Round 2 seat allotment results for UGMAC 2026, the state counselling process for undergraduate AYUSH courses. Candidates who have been allotted seats in Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery (BAMS), Bachelor of Homoeopathic Medicine and Surgery (BHMS), or Bachelor of Unani Medicine and Surgery (BUMS) programmes must now complete document verification and formal admission at their assigned colleges. The reporting window is tight—just three days, from September 27 to 29, 2026—and missing this deadline will result in forfeiture of the allotted seat. This round offers a second opportunity for NEET UG 2026 qualifiers who did not secure a seat in Round 1 or wish to upgrade to a better college or course. If you have been allotted an AYUSH seat in Bihar UGMAC 2026 Round 2, you must report to your college and complete document verification by September 29, 2026, or your seat will be cancelled. What is Bihar UGMAC 2026 Round 2 and who can apply? UGMAC 2026 is Bihar's state-level counselling process for undergraduate AYUSH courses. It allocates seats in BAMS, BHMS, and BUMS programmes across government and private colleges in the state. Round 2 was opened after seats remained vacant following the first round of allotment, giving candidates a fresh opportunity to secure admission. To be eligible for Round 2, you must have qualified the NEET UG 2026 examination and hold valid Bihar domicile status. You must also have passed Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology as core subjects, along with English as a required subject. Additionally, you must have already registered for UGMAC 2026 counselling during the initial registration window. Age limits follow the guidelines set by the National Medical Commission. How is seat allotment decided in UGMAC 2026? Seat allotment in UGMAC 2026 is based on two primary factors: your NEET UG 2026 score and the choices you filled during the counselling registration process. The merit list is prepared using your NEET score, and seats are allocated in order of merit according to your preference list. This means the college and course you receive depend on your rank, the number of available seats, and how you ranked your choices. If you did not receive a seat in Round 1, Round 2 gives you another chance. Candidates can also use Round 2 to upgrade—that is, move from a lower-ranked college to a higher-ranked one, or from a less preferred course to a more preferred one, if their merit position allows. Key dates and reporting window for Round 2 The allotment results were declared on September 25, 2026, and are available on the official BCECEB portal at bceceboard.bihar.gov.in. Once you know your allotted college and course, you have a very limited window to complete the next steps: document verification and admission must be completed between September 27 and September 29, 2026. bihar_raw_news.title: After Jamui, now molestation cases in 2 more Bihar districts - The Navhind Times
bihar_raw_news.content: SHARE Patna: Days after the horrific molestation case in Bihar’s Jamui district, a girl was allegedly harassed in public by a group of people in Samastipur and a minor was “sexually assaulted” in Muzaffarpur, prompting the Opposition to target the BJP-led NDA government over the law and order situation. The fresh incidents led to the arrest of altogether five persons, police said on Thursday. In Samastipur, the police arrested four persons who have been booked under relevant sections of the BNS, besides the IT Act and POCSO Act, after a video went viral on social media in which they could be seen molesting the girl. According to a statement issued by Samastipur police, the video “appears about a week old” and the victim was “yet to be identified”, though a case was lodged under the aforementioned laws since “the girl looked like a minor and the matter was sensitive”. Three of the accused, Vikas Kumar, Rahul Kumar and Rambabu Sahni, were residents of Jagatsinghpur village, where the incident had taken place, while the fourth, Awadhesh Paswan, hailed from Bijaulia. In adjoining Muzaffarpur, police arrested one Lalit Kumar, who had allegedly molested and beaten up a girl in the Town police station area. According to the Muzaffarpur police, the accused appeared to be mentally unstable, and his condition was being investigated by experts while the victim has been admitted to the Sadar Hospital for treatment. Police also debunked rumours on social media that a similar incident had taken place in Madhepura. According to the Madhepura police, a video that was being circulated was shot near a secondary school, and the students, male and female, were engaged in a heated debate after half-yearly examinations. The Madhepura police also said it will take action against “those who shared the video on social media with ulterior motives”. Meanwhile, the fresh incidents led to fresh attacks on the state’s BJP-led government from Opposition leaders like RJD working president Tejashwi Yadav and Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor. Yadav, who is the leader of the Opposition in the state assembly, linked the worsening law and order with alleged criminal antecedents of Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary. He also shared a video of minister Ashok Choudhary, claiming that the outbursts of the senior JD(U) leader were “a clear signal of administrative chaos that engulfs Bihar”. Ashok Choudhary, whose daughter Shambhavi is, incidentally, the LJPRV MP from Samastipur, can be heard saying the incidents in Bihar should not be fretted about as crimes against women took place “in highly advanced countries like America and Japan”. bihar_raw_news.title: Banwarilal Chandiwala Launches All-India Franchise Model and "Jewellery on Wheels"
bihar_raw_news.content: Home / Content / Specials / Bihar Creates History - Banwarilal Chandiwala Launches All-India Franchise Model and "Jewellery on Wheels" Bihar Creates History - Banwarilal Chandiwala Launches All-India Franchise Model and "Jewellery on Wheels" A Bihar-origin speciality accessories concept expands through franchising while taking accessories directly to customers India's biggest Silver mall 3 min read Last Updated : Sep 25 2026 | 3:12 PM IST Patna: Banwarilal Chandiwala — India’s largest hallmark silver ornaments mall — is rapidly expanding beyond Bihar and moving towards establishing its presence across the country. The company has initiated its national expansion under its All-India Franchise Model, marking a new phase in its retail journey. The growth is designed to take the brand’s distinctive precious metal shopping journey to customers in more cities while creating opportunities for business partners across the country. With its focus on hallmarked collections and a wider collection of product portfolio, the company is positioning itself around an organised, contemporary approach to specialised commerce. Three Partner Outlets Finalised, With More Cities Identified A key highlight of this expansion is that three partner outlets have already been finalised. At the same time, major cities across the state, including Boring Road in Patna, Gaya, Muzaffarpur, Bhagalpur, Darbhanga, Purnia, Ara, Begusarai, Katihar, Munger, Chhapra and Samastipur, along with other prominent cities across India, have been identified for outlet expansion. The proposed expansion reflects the brand’s intention to build a wider marketplace network while retaining the identity and product focus that originated in Bihar. The partnership model is expected to help bring the brand’s hallmark ornaments and premium offerings closer to customers in different markets. “Jewellery on Wheels” — Taking Luxury Shopping on the Road As part of this expansion and innovation journey, the company has also launched “Jewellery on Wheels.” The concept introduces a mobile showroom format, allowing customers to experience accessory shopping beyond a conventional fixed store location. “Bihar creates a world-first — India’s first luxury jewellery experience on wheels.” Customers will now be able to enjoy a unique shopping experience featuring hallmarked pieces and premium products not only at the grand flagship mall but also aboard the Jewellery on Wheels bus. The concept brings together Accessories, Mobility, and Luxury Shopping, creating a new-age shopping experience. Currently, the mobile showroom concept is operational in Patna, while the company has also begun offering franchise opportunities. As the franchise network grows, the concept is intended to support the brand’s wider expansion and potentially bring the mobile ornaments experience to more cities across India. A Complete Product Experience The Banwarilal Chandiwala mall offers an extensive collection of premium products, including hallmark precious metal ornaments, artefacts, gifting items, decorative pieces and silver furniture. The broader product offering is designed to demonstrate the versatility of the precious metal beyond traditional ornaments, covering gifting, décor and lifestyle categories as well. The mall was inaugurated by renowned storyteller and spiritual speaker Jaya Kishori Ji, adding to the significance of the brand’s launch in Bihar. Taking a Bihar-Origin Retail Identity Nationwide

bihar_raw_news.title: New Amrit Bharat Express to Connect Gujarat, Rajasthan, UP and Bihar
bihar_raw_news.content: New Amrit Bharat Express to Connect Gujarat, Rajasthan, UP and Bihar Indian Railways has approved the introduction of a new tri-weekly Amrit Bharat Express between Bhuj in Gujarat and Barauni in Bihar By Razia Sanwari | Sep 25, 2026, 13:02 IST Join for live updates on WhatsApp UdaipurTimes, Sept 25, 2026 - Indian Railways has approved the introduction of a new tri-weekly Amrit Bharat Express between Bhuj in Gujarat and Barauni in Bihar. The new service will cover a distance of 2,532 km, connecting important destinations across Gujarat, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. Service Three Days a Week Train No. 19427 Bhuj-Barauni Amrit Bharat Express will depart from Bhuj at 17:30 hours and reach Barauni at 04:05 hours. In the return direction, Train No. 19428 Barauni-Bhuj Amrit Bharat Express will depart Barauni at 23:55 hours and reach Bhuj at 13:15 hours. The Bhuj-Barauni service will operate on Monday, Wednesday and Saturday, while the Barauni-Bhuj service will operate on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday. Stations Connected The new service will have commercial stoppages at several important stations en route, including Samakhiali, Ahmedabad, Ratlam, Kota, Sawai Madhopur, Gangapur City, Bharatpur, Mathura, Hathras, Bareilly, Izzatnagar, Pilibhit, Lakhimpur, Gonda, Gorakhpur, Siwan, Chhapra, Hajipur, Muzaffarpur and Samastipur, among others. The new train service will provide an additional rail travel option between western and eastern parts of the country and improve connectivity for passengers travelling between Gujarat, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. bihar_raw_news.title: India Infrastructure Push: How Expressways, Vande Bharat Trains Cut Travel Time
bihar_raw_news.content: India’s Infrastructure Revolution 2026: Check Key Vande Bharat, Bullet Trains, Expressways, Tunnel Routes; Travel Time Reduced to Minutes By Jaisal Kaur Last Updated: Sep 25, 2026, 13:40 IST Bridges have massively improved connectivity across rivers and rough terrain. The Bhupen Hazarika Setu, also known as the Dhola-Sadiya Bridge, reduced travel between Rupai in Assam and Meka/Roing in Arunachal Pradesh from around six hours to one hour As per government data quoted in recent reports, the Delhi-Mumbai road journey is targeted to fall from 33 to 12 hours, while Delhi-Katra travel reduces from 14 to 6 hours. India’s broadening network of expressways, bridges, tunnels and faster trains is decreasing travel times across major routes. Projects charted to bypass geographical barriers, reduce detours and bolster rail speeds are putting several long-distance journeys within shorter travel spans. According to government data quoted in recent reports, the Delhi-Mumbai road journey is targeted to fall from about 33 hours to 12 hours, while Delhi-Katra travel is slated to reduce from 14 hours to six hours. Bridges reduce long journeys Bridges have massively improved connectivity across rivers and rough terrain. The Bhupen Hazarika Setu, also known as the Dhola-Sadiya Bridge, reduced travel between Rupai in Assam and Meka/Roing in Arunachal Pradesh from around six hours to one hour. The Bogibeel Bridge has lowered the travel time between Dhemaji and Dibrugarh to almost a day to around one to two hours. In Bihar, the Kosi Rail Mahasetu reduced the Nirmali-Saraigarh rail journey from about eight hours to 30 minutes, while cutting the rail distance from nearly 300 km to around 22 km. Tunnels bypass difficult terrain Mountain tunnels are also cutting down travel distances and offering more reliable connectivity. The 9.02-km Atal Tunnel bypasses the Rohtang Pass, cutting around 46 km from the route and saving approximately four to five hours. The Dr Syama Prasad Mookerjee Tunnel has lowered the Jammu-Srinagar road distance by about 30 km and saves nearly two hours. The Banihal-Qazigund twin-tube tunnel saves around 1.5 hours, while the Sela Tunnel has reduced travel time on the Tezpur-Tawang route by more than an hour. Expressways shorten road journeys Access-controlled highways are causing major reductions on inter-city routes. The Delhi-Meerut Expressway has brought travel time down from around 2.5 hours to about 50 minutes. The Bengaluru-Mysuru route has dipped from nearly three hours to around 75 minutes. Moreover, the Delhi-Dehradun Economic Corridor has reduced journey time from more than six hours to about 2.5 hours. Meanwhile, the Delhi-Amritsar-Katra Expressway is aimed at reducing Delhi-Amritsar travel from eight hours to four hours, and Delhi-Katra travel from 14 hours to six hours. The Delhi-Mumbai Expressway is being constructed to bring the journey from roughly 33 hours to about 12 hours. Vande Bharat adds speed to rail travel Indian Railways is also reducing journey times by upgrading present services and launching faster trains. bihar_raw_news.title: Village infrastructure improved significantly, urban-rural gap narrowed in 12 years: PM Modi
bihar_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Photo |ANI India Village infrastructure improved significantly, urban-rural gap narrowed in 12 years: PM Modi Modi said the country had also witnessed greater self-reliance among women since his government came to power in 2014. TNIE online desk Updated: 25th Sep, 2026 at 10:47 AM Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said the gap between urban and rural India had narrowed significantly over the past 12 years, with village infrastructure witnessing substantial improvement. Interacting with participants of the ongoing 'Seva Yatra' motorcycle rally from Varanasi to Vadnagar, Modi said the country had also witnessed greater self-reliance among women since his government came to power in 2014. "Over the past 12 years, the gap between cities and villages in India has significantly narrowed. Today, infrastructure in villages has improved significantly," Modi said. He said efforts towards social reform and positive change should continue irrespective of electoral considerations and stressed the need to work beyond "vote bank politics". Two motorcycle rallies were flagged off on September 17, Modi's 76th birthday, from Vadnagar in Gujarat and Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh. The rallies, which are scheduled to conclude on October 7, are being held to mark 25 years of Modi's public service. Vadnagar, where Modi was born, and Varanasi, which he has represented in the Lok Sabha since 2014, are the two endpoints of the rallies. The rallies are passing through towns, districts and villages, taking the message of service to grassroots communities while bringing together youth participation, social welfare, cultural engagement and community mobilisation. Modi said Vadnagar had given him the values that shaped his life, while Kashi had added "countless colours of service" to those values. On Thursday, Modi had interacted with participants of the rally travelling from Vadnagar to Varanasi. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that Viksit Bharat can be realised only with the contribution and participation of everyone. Mr Modi made these remarks during a virtual interaction with Seva Yatris travelling on the Yatra from Varanasi to Vadnagar under Seva Sankalp Abhiyan. Mr Modi highlighted that Vadnagar gave him the values that shaped his life, while Kashi added countless colours of service to those values. He expressed happiness that young people are also enriching this journey with the many colours of service. The Prime Minister noted that over the past 12 years, the gap between cities and villages in India has narrowed significantly. Today, infrastructure in villages has improved considerably, while self-reliance among the women of the country has also increased. Mr Modi said that today marks the birth anniversary of Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya. He highlighted the seven principles given by Pandit Upadhyaya of service, balance, patience, coordination, positivity, sensitivity and dialogue. He added that every BJP worker takes pride in following the path shown by Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya with a spirit of service. During the interaction these yatris shared their experiences with the Prime Minister. Mr Modi also urged the yatris to maintain a diary and record their experiences during the Yatra.

national_raw_news.title: 25 mins ago | Regional News 35 Flood-like conditions emerge in southern Odisha amid heavy rain
national_raw_news.content: The depression over South Odisha is continuing to cause heavy rain across several parts of the state. Flood-like conditions have emerged in southern Odisha, with rivers rising and road communication disrupted in several districts. The system is likely to weaken further during the next twelve hours, but heavy rain is expected to continue in vulnerable areas. Akashvani correspondent reports that in Malkangiri, several major bridges and roads are submerged, cutting off road communication with neighbouring districts and Andhra Pradesh. Water is flowing over bridges on National Highway 326, while landslides and uprooted trees have further disrupted connectivity. Disaster response teams are working round the clock to clear blocked roads. In south Odisha, rivers are rising amid incessant rain, creating flood-like conditions. Five sluice gates of the Indravati Dam have been opened to release excess water. In north Odisha, many low-lying areas are under the threat of flooding due to rising rivers. The government says there is no immediate threat from the Brahmani and Mahanadi. However, the Budhabalanga, Bansadhara, Naluha and Rushikulya rivers are in spate. The Bansadhara is above the danger level at Kashinagar. The depression is weakening over land, but the India Meteorological Department has forecast heavy rain today in Malkangiri, Koraput and Kalahandi.

national_raw_news.title: 25 mins ago | National 218 Despite global uncertainties, India achieved 7.8 % growth rate: Union Minister Amit Shah at UP In...
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah has said that despite global uncertainties, India has achieved a 7.8 percent growth rate and is maintaining its position as the fastest-growing major economy. Inaugurating the Uttar Pradesh International Trade Show UPITS at Greater Noida this afternoon, Mr Shah cited robust global indicators for India. He noted that Moody’s has upgraded India’s growth forecast, while Japan’s JCR has elevated the nation’s sovereign rating. Mr Shah stated that the country is moving forward with the resolve of Viksit Bharat by 2047. He said exports have witnessed a manifold increase and there has been rapid progress in the semiconductor sector. Lauding the Yogi Adityanath-led government, Mr Shah said, strict law and order, combined with favourable industrial policies and proactive governance, has created a highly attractive investment environment in Uttar Pradesh today. He said investments in the defence sector are flowing into Uttar Pradesh through the defence corridor. The Home Minister said the BrahMos missile system being manufactured in the state and the AK-203 rifles being produced in Amethi highlight the state’s new role in defence production. Mr Shah stated that the Noida Airport, expressways, and improved connectivity reflect the changing industrial landscape of Uttar Pradesh. He noted that the state is now advancing in the sectors of investment, industry, and manufacturing and is poised to move towards the goal of becoming a one trillion dollar economy. In his address, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said that the state has emerged as the manufacturing hub in the country. He highlighted the participation of Japan, Vietnam, Russia, Singapore, Austria, and Belarus as partner countries in the UPITS 2026. The Chief Minister noted that their special pavilions are elevating bilateral trade commitments to new heights, paving the way for strategic partnerships, technology transfers, and joint ventures. He emphasised that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India has signed Free Trade Agreements with major global economies, which Uttar Pradesh is actively leveraging. He added that the significant presence of international buyers at the event is a clear indicator of global trust in the quality of the state’s products, its robust supply chain, and the credibility of its entrepreneurs. The Chief Minister informed that over two thousand 400 exhibitors are currently participating in the sprawling 36 thousand-square-meter export center.

national_raw_news.title: 6 hours ago | National 141 Make in India initiative completes 12 years
national_raw_news.content: Today marks 12 years of Make in India. It was on this day in 2014 that the initiative was launched with the ambition of becoming a global hub for manufacturing, design and innovation. The initiative has transformed India’s manufacturing landscape by expanding production, investment and capabilities across industries. Akashvani correspondent reports that over the years, Make in India has opened new opportunities for businesses and investors to participate in India’s manufacturing journey. The initiative has subsequently been expanded under Make in India 2.0. The initiative now focuses on 27 sectors, which include 15 in manufacturing and 12 in services. The initiative focused on facilitating investment, fostering innovation and developing world-class infrastructure. Guided by ‘Minimum Government, Maximum Governance’, it has also sought to modernise processes and policies. Under the initiative, India’s electronics production increased nearly sevenfold, from 1.9 lakh crore rupees in 2014-15 to over 13 lakh crore in 2025-26. Mobile-phone production rose approximately 33-fold, from 18 thousand crore to 6.27 lakh crore over the same period. During this period, Indian Railways manufactured nearly 55 thousand coaches over 2014-24, while average annual railway coach production rose from less than 3 thousand 300 during 2004-14 to over 5 thousand during 2014-24. Over 6 thousand 6 hundred Linke Hofmann Busch (LHB) coaches were manufactured in 2025-26. Further, under the Make in India initiative, the country’s indigenous defence production increased from 46 thousand 429 crore in 2014-15 to a record 1.78 lakh crore in Financial Year 2025-26, bringing production to nearly four times its 2014-15 level. The initiative now goes beyond producing more goods and focuses on building the skills, technology and capacity needed to make them in India.

Daily Excelsior 04:04 AM Sep 25, 2026 IST Members of Bhopal media delegation with scientists at CSIR-IIIM Jammu. Excelsior Correspondent JAMMU, Sept 24: A media delegation from Bhopal, on an exposure tour organized by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), today visited CSIR–Indian Institute of Integrative Medicine (CSIR-IIIM), Jammu, and Border Outpost (BOP) Suchetgarh to gain first-hand insight into scientific research, innovation, border management and tourism initiatives. At CSIR-IIIM, the visiting journalists interacted with scientists and officials and were briefed on the Institute’s research, societal mission projects and bio-entrepreneurship initiatives. Welcoming the delegation, Dr Saurabh Saran highlighted the Institute’s advanced facilities and industry linkages, describing CSIR-IIIM as a bridge connecting industries, startups, farmers, youth, academic institutions and Government agencies. He said the institute was pursuing drug leads for challenging conditions, including Alzheimer’s disease, osteoarthritis and cancer pain, by integrating traditional Ayurveda with modern medicine. Advertisement Dr Suphla Gupta, Senior Principal Scientist and Nodal Officer for the CSIR Aroma Mission, briefed the delegation on the Aroma Mission, Floriculture Mission and Bioresource Conservation & Prospection initiatives. She also highlighted the JIGYASA programme aimed at exposing students to advanced scientific equipment and technical processes. Dr Amit Nargotra, Senior Principal Scientist, explained the work being undertaken at the Plant Science Laboratory, including studies of chemical compounds derived from medicinal and aromatic plants. Anil Kumar Katare, Senior Principal Scientist, outlined drug formulation protocols and the screening of candidates for safety, efficacy and toxicity. Dr Vidushi Abrol, Business Manager, BioNEST IIIM-Technology Business Incubator (TBI), briefed the delegation on incubation support aimed at promoting entrepreneurship and sustainable employment opportunities, particularly in J&K. Later, at Suchetgarh BOP, the delegation interacted with BSF personnel and was briefed by senior officers on round-the-clock border management and the multi-layered security grid along the International Border. Officers also explained border tourism initiatives aimed at showcasing border life, the role and sacrifices of security forces and creating livelihood opportunities for local residents. Officials said Suchetgarh has emerged as a prominent patriotic tourism destination, attracting nearly 1,500 visitors daily on weekdays, while weekend footfall rises to around 2,000–4,000 visitors per day.
